prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a high-angle downward view inside a compact bathroom where the camera wearer stands directly behind and above a shirtless seated person whose head is about 0.4–0.6 m away and whose torso and chair back are about 0.7–0.9 m below, with a pedestal sink to the lower left at roughly 0.8–1.0 m and a bathtub in front of the seated person at 1.2–1.6 m. The camera wearer's own hands, holding wired hair clippers and their cord within immediate arm's reach at 0.2–0.5 m, appear brightest in the foreground, while the seated person faces away toward the bathtub and holds a smartphone in front of their chest at about 0.8–0.9 m from the camera. Across the five frames, the wearer's right hand and clippers move from touching the top of the seated person's head in frame 1 to the right side of the head in frame 2, retreat downward to the lower right in frames 3–4 while the left hand enters at the bottom left holding the cord, and in frame 5 the left hand holds the clippers at the bottom left while the right hand reaches forward to touch the crown of the head, partly occluding it. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the vertical layering between the wearer's foreground hands, the thin clipper cord, the seated person's head and shoulders, and the deeper basin of the bathtub. However, the map is unreliable inside the white bathtub where the smooth surface collapses into a uniform black void with lost fixture geometry, and along the clipper body and cord where depth bleeds into the adjacent skin and background.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map labels parts of the scene into foreground people and background bathroom fixtures, placing the seated person in the lower center at roughly 0.4–0.9 m from the camera wearer, a pedestal sink to the lower left at about 0.8–1.0 m (and ~0.3 m left of the seated person), and the bathtub ahead at 1.2–1.6 m. The seated person sits on a chair facing away from the camera wearer and slightly left toward the sink/bathtub corner, never looking toward the camera, while both the seated person's head and the clipper assembly remain within the camera wearer's arm's reach and the smartphone stays within the seated person's reach. Across the five frames, the camera wearer's right arm moves from the upper right over the head in frames 1–2, drops largely out of the lower frame in frames 3–4, and reaches back over the head in frame 5, partially occluding the seated person's hair and right shoulder. The map makes instance boundaries between the seated person and the background sink and tub walls explicit in frames 1–2, which can blend in peripheral RGB views. However, it is highly unreliable: it misclassifies the bathtub as a 'sink' in every frame, mislabels the hair clippers as a 'cell phone' in frame 2, merges the camera wearer's hands and clippers into the seated person's mask in frames 1 and 3–4, and in frame 5 fails to segment the seated person's head and upper back entirely while labeling only the wearer's foreground hands and forearms as 'person'.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders 2D skeletal keypoints on a black background, isolating the seated person's torso and limb configuration at 0.5–0.9 m below and in front of the camera wearer alongside the camera wearer's own hands at 0.2–0.5 m. In frames 2, 3, and 4, yellow torso and upper-leg lines show the seated person oriented away from the camera wearer and angled toward the upper-left sink/bathtub area, with their left arm bent forward holding the phone and their head keypoints clustered near the neck without facing the camera. Across the sequence, the magenta hand skeleton tracks the camera wearer's right hand within arm's reach as it moves from above the seated person's head in frame 1, down to the right side of the head in frame 2, disappears in frames 3–4 when the wearer's hands drop to the lower edge of the view, and reappears on top of the head in frame 5. This skeletal overlay reveals the underlying shoulder, hip, knee, and bent left-arm geometry of the seated person in frames 3–4 despite foreshortening and partial occlusion by the head, torso, and clipper cord in the RGB image. However, the pose map is unreliable in several places: it completely misses the seated person's body skeleton in frames 1 and 5, fails to detect the camera wearer's hands at the bottom of frames 3–4 and left hand in frame 5, and places noisy facial keypoints on the back of the seated person's head in frames 2–4 as if they were facing forward.
